author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A broad single-volume sampler of Dick's short fiction, chosen to represent his range across reality slippage, android empathy, and small men against systems, and preserved here in two archive editions.
page_summary:
The Philip K. Dick Reader is a representative gathering of Dick's short stories, drawn from his large body of magazine work and assembled to give a reader the breadth of his short fiction in one book. It includes several of the pieces that became films, alongside stories better known to devotees than to filmgoers.

The selection foregrounds the concerns that run through all of Dick's work: reality breaking down under scrutiny, the android or simulacrum that tests the boundary of the human, betrayal within apparently ordinary relationships, and the individual dwarfed by systems of power. Read as a whole, it shows how consistently Dick pursued these questions and how many forms he found for them.

The QueryPat archive preserves this work across two manifestations, letting edition history and republication be read together. As an entry point, the Reader is a strong first encounter with Dick's short fiction and its recurring machinery of doubt.
